evidence: Two top-level packages ('treenode' and 'tests') indicate clear separation of concerns
'treenode' contains logically grouped submodules (models, admin, forms, signals, utils, cache, etc.), suggesting cohesive internal modules
All functionality resides within a single Python package with no external service boundaries or inter-process communication
Django ORM and built-in patterns (models.Model, admin.ModelAdmin) used consistently within the core library
No evidence of remote APIs, message queues, or external adapters — all adapters (e.g., admin, signals) are internal to the app
Modular organization with dedicated modules for persistence (models), persistence caching (cache), memory debugging (memory), signal handling (signals), etc., typical of modular monoliths
High internal cohesion and low coupling between modules (e.g., utils and exceptions used by multiple layers without tight dependencies)
risks: Lack of strict layered separation (e.g., admin directly interacts with model internals), blurring layer boundaries
Risk of technical debt if internal module dependencies become cyclic over time
Limited scalability via horizontal partitioning — all components deploy together
